first_impression: This looks lovely and it clearly knows what it is: chunky low-poly sheep, a warm storybook UI, a sunset that actually turns into a moonlit night. It has more structure than I expected for an itch game, a season map, charms, ribbons and a daily evening. My doubt is whether the high camera and the samey yellow ground make the middle evenings blur together.
best_things: The low view in e1-low-view.jpg (Pip in the foreground, the stream, the bridge and pink haze behind) is a store-page screenshot all by itself and makes the valley feel like a real place.

Every evening adds one clear new idea, spelled out on a handsome card: lambs, Old Angus the ram, a sheepdog trial scored on points, a night watch until dawn, mist, a storm and flood, snow, plus a harder Wolf Moon version (wolf-moon-card.jpg).

The day-to-night arc is a real event: the bar fills from gold to violet, the light goes rose then blue, and the night watch going from moonlit blue (evening-5-night.jpg) to green morning (evening-5-dawn.jpg) feels earned.

worst_problems.problem: The wolf, the one thing I should be watching, keeps showing up as a small blob in the dark pine line at the very bottom of the screen, half under the stamina and controls bar, while the banner says 'A wolf is stalking your flock!'. The camera frames Pip and the fold and leaves the threat at the edge.
worst_problems.suggestion: When a wolf is stalking, pull the camera so the wolf is in the open part of the screen, or at least lift the HUD bar out of the way. Do not let the scariest thing in the game hide behind my stamina meter.

worst_problems.problem: Too many things look like sheep. At night the round white moonlit boulders with dark tops look exactly like sheep lying down; in the snow the snow-capped rocks and shrubs on the left look like a second flock; in the mist the real sheep look like grey boulders.
worst_problems.suggestion: Keep rocks dark and flat-topped, no white caps that read as fleece, and give the sheep one thing that never changes (a face, a cream glow, a little outline) so I can always count my flock at a glance.

worst_problems.problem: The places are not as different as the cards promise. Mist on the Moor, The Gathering and First Snow all start at the same stepping-stone crossing with the same minimap, and Lambing Time, Old Angus, the trial and the Gathering are all the same mustard-gold ground seen from straight above.
worst_problems.where: evening-6-mist.jpg, evening-9-gather.jpg, evening-8-snow.jpg, evening-3-lambing.jpg, evening-4-angus.jpg, evening-5-trial.jpg
worst_problems.suggestion: Give each place its own look from the play camera, not just on the title card: a loch shore with sand and reeds, a rocky corrie, a real pass with cliffs. And start the High Pass evenings somewhere different each time.

worst_problems.problem: The storm looks murky and empty: a dark green-grey field, no sheep in view, the stream reads as a black tarmac road, and Pip seen from straight above is just a black and white pill.
worst_problems.suggestion: Show some sheep and lightning flashes on screen, make the stream look like water (foam, a lighter edge), and tilt the camera a little so Pip still looks like a dog when he runs up the screen.

worst_problems.problem: The night watch star targets make no sense: one star for losing 1 or fewer, two stars for 0, three stars for none. Two and three stars are the same thing.
worst_problems.suggestion: Make the tiers different, for example one star for losing 2 or fewer, two for 1, three for none, or tie the third star to something else like no rescues needed.

boredom_points: The trial (evening-5-trial.jpg) is five sheep on a flat empty yellow field. The card says the whole glen is watching, but I see no crowd, no judges, nothing but the gates.
The Gathering asks for 18 of 22 with 6:39 on the clock (evening-9-gather.jpg). A long drove of the same herding on the same yellow ground could drag.

The opening of evening 1 already has a wolf stalking at the edge with 1:32 left (e1-first-home.jpg), and the next three shots look almost the same. If the camera stays this high, much of the evening is watching a small flock shuffle towards a fold.
confusions: The orange and white dog next to Pip in evening-9-gather.jpg is apparently Old Fly, but from above she looks like a fox, and the wolves are the enemy here. I would hesitate before trusting her.
Old Fly comes free in The Gathering, but she is also a charm that costs 16 stars on the season map. Is she earned or given?
The 'Quiet dog' ribbon is greyed out on the evening 1 result (evening-1-result.jpg) with no line saying I failed it or why.
Several season map titles are cut off ('Lambing', 'The Glenbrae', 'The Gatherin') in season-map.jpg.
In evening-3-lambing.jpg I cannot spot the lambs in the flock at all; they look like slightly smaller sheep.
wish_list: An option to play from the low tilted view, or a camera that tilts more when I zoom in, because that view is the best-looking thing in the game.
A visible crowd and a judge at the trial, and a score breakdown per gate at the end.
Some reward I can see on Pip or the farm as the season goes on (the 'Pip's coat' section hints at it, show it off more).
A photo mode for that sunset.
one_line_review: A gorgeous, cosy sheepdog season with real structure and a sunset worth staying up for, held back by wolves hiding at the screen edge and too many evenings on the same yellow grass.
